- **Builder:** Crazy Tube Circuits
- **Catalog identity:** Falcon - Overdrive
- **Catalog type:** Overdrive / Amp-in-a-Box
- **Identity:** Exact Crazy Tube Circuits Falcon.

Falcon is a JFET-based amp-in-a-box overdrive designed to recreate the behavior of two classic Fender amplifier circuits: the **1955 Tweed Deluxe / 5E3** and **1961 Brownface Princeton / 6G2**. Crazy Tube Circuits describes the design as reproducing the preamp, phase inverter and power-amp behavior, including the compression and sag associated with the original tube power sections and rectifiers.

- **Volume:** controls the amount of gain/drive.
- **Tone:** shapes the high-frequency response; lower settings smooth the sound while higher settings add upper-frequency emphasis and additional gain.
- **Output:** controls the final output level and can be set to match bypass level or provide additional boost.
- **'55 / '61 toggle:** selects between the Tweed Deluxe and Brownface Princeton voicings.

- True bypass.
- 9V DC center-negative external supply.
- Published current-draw figures vary by source and production listing, so an exact factory current value is not asserted here.

- **'55 Tweed mode:** higher gain, more low-end response, and greater power-amp compression/sag.
- **'61 Brownface mode:** lower gain with a tighter, more focused low end.
- These are the two documented amplifier voicings inside the same Falcon model, not separate catalog pedals.

No distinct production circuit revision was established in the checked sources. The documented '55 and '61 modes are the core design feature.

- JFET technology is explicitly documented.
- Exact JFET part number(s) were not established from reliable manufacturer or independent sources, so third-party unverified component claims are excluded.

- Exact diode type or part number: **not established**.

The Falcon is designed to move from dynamic low-gain breakup toward expressive tweed-style overdrive. The '55 side has more gain, low end and compression, while the '61 side is cleaner, tighter and more focused. Independent GuitarPlayer coverage notes strong touch dynamics, responsive cleanup with guitar volume, and distinct tweed/brownface behavior between the two modes.

- Handmade in Greece.
- Compact stompbox format.
- Crazy Tube Circuits describes the Falcon as an analog/JFET recreation of the two source amplifiers.

- Exact-model manufacturer: https://crazytubecircuits.com/falcon

sources.h1: Crazy Tube Circuits introduces the Falcon
sources.excerpt:
Crazy Tube Circuits introduces the Falcon | Guitar.com News Reviews Guides Features Magazine Tuner Deals Related Brands Crazy Tube Circuits Related Tags # Distortion # Effects When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more Featured Deal Fender Custom Shop Madison '54 Telecaster Masterbuilt by Greg Fessler – save nearly $3,000 Claim News Crazy Tube Circuits introduces the Falcon An overdrive pedal modelled after two legendary amps. by Guitar.com December 13, 2018 by Guitar.com December 13, 2018 When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more Want more news stories from Guitar.com ? Follow us on Google News. Crazy Tube Circuits has unveiled the Falcon, an overdrive pedal that takes cues from the ’55 Tweed Deluxe and the ’61 Brownface Princeton amps. In 2016, the Athens-based company created a custom amp that could morph between the tones of the aforementioned amps. With the Falcon, the brand is aiming to capture that feature in pedal form. Using JFET technology, Crazy Tube Circuits has managed to recreate the behaviour, sound and feel of the two amps. A vital part of this was emulating the compression and sag of the power amp and tube rectifier, respectively. These components contribute to the pedal’s responsiveness, dynamic and musical quality. Here’s a quick look at the pedal’s controls: Amp Mode switch : ’55 (Tweed): Has more gain, greater low-end response, and a higher sag/compression ’61 (Brownface): Has a lower gain that produces slightly overdriven sounds Volume knob : Controls the amount of gain Tone knob : Below noon: Smoothens tone Past noon: Boosts upper frequencies and injects extra gain Output knob : Manages output volume. Can be configured to match bypass level or to boost an amp Check out the pedal in action here: Retails at €169. More information at crazytubecircuits.com .
